# elves_client_rule (Resource)

Includes or excludes a rule for one Mac (client), by serial number. Rules set on the Mac itself are applied last, after its configuration, SCIM group and SCIM user rules, so they win over all of them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Allow a tool on one Mac only
resource "elves_client_rule" "build_mac_tool" {
  serial_number = "C02XK0AAJG5J"
  rule_id       = elves_rule.build_tool.id
  action        = "include"
}

# Lift a rule that this Mac gets from its configuration or a group
resource "elves_client_rule" "build_mac_no_block" {
  serial_number = "C02XK0AAJG5J"
  rule_id       = elves_rule.blocked_tool.id
  action        = "exclude"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `rule_id` (Number) Required. ID of the rule to assign, for example `elves_rule.example.id`. Changing it replaces the assignment.
- `serial_number` (String) Required. Serial number of the Mac, as shown on the Elves Clients page. The Mac must have synced with Elves at least once. Changing it replaces the assignment.

### Optional

- `action` (String) Optional. `include` adds the rule. `exclude` takes it away when an earlier level adds it: rules are applied as default rules, then the configuration, then SCIM groups, then the SCIM user, then the Mac itself. Defaults to `include`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the assignment, `<serial_number>/<rule_id>`. Used for import.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A client rule can be imported by specifying <serial_number>/<rule_id>.
terraform import elves_client_rule.example C02XK0AAJG5J/68
```
